summary: Tested the 3 new enhancements: BOM Explorer column sorting + text search, and Purchasing Plan month picker + Excel export. Search, highlighting, month-picker (incl. past months), and Excel export mechanics all work correctly. Found ONE real bug: sorting the BOM tree corrupts the expand/collapse state of sub-assemblies, causing children to randomly appear/disappear after a sort click.

ui_bugs.issue: expandedKeys (and effectiveExpandedKeys used for rendering children) are positional index-path strings (e.g. '1', '2') computed once via collectExpandableKeys(result.tree) in ORIGINAL tree order. sortTree() reorders siblings, so a node's path in the rendered displayTree changes after sorting, but the Set of expanded paths does NOT get remapped to the node's new position. Result: after clicking a sort header, previously-expanded sub-assemblies can silently collapse (or the wrong node ends up 'expanded') because the stored path no longer points to the same node.

action_items: Fix BomExplorerPage.js: expand/collapse state must be tracked by a stable node identity (e.g. product_id + ancestor product_id chain, or product_uuid) instead of positional index path, so it survives re-ordering from sortTree(). Reproduction: load BOM P26584 -> Expand All (P26688 and P26680 sub-assemblies both expanded, 7 rows visible) -> click 'Quantity' header once (ascending): only 5 rows render, BOTH P26688's child (ROD-9) and P26680's child (SH6.0HR) disappear even though the toggle carets still visually show as if state didn't change for those rows. Click 'Quantity' header again (descending): 6 rows render, showing P26680's child SH6.0HR but still NOT P26688's child ROD-9. Expected: both sub-assemblies should remain expanded (7 rows total) across both sorts, since sorting should only reorder siblings, not affect expand state.
critical_code_review_comments: filterTree/highlightMatch/sortTree helpers are clean and correctly handle nested recursion; search auto-expand via effectiveExpandedKeys = collectExpandableKeys(displayTree) when treeSearch is set works well and is not affected by the sort-state bug (search always force-expands everything).

Backend: _validate_month() correctly enforces YYYY-MM regex; build_purchasing_plan raises a clear ValueError for invalid months, which the async job wraps into job status 'failed' with a readable error message - verified via direct API test with '2026-13'.
Backend: no restriction on past months in _validate_month/_default_month - confirmed a past month (2020-01) generates a valid single-month plan end-to-end.

PurchasingPlanPage.js: month input correctly disabled while loading; export button correctly disabled until plan is set; filename PurchasingPlan_<month>.xlsx and sheet names (Purchasing Plan / Missing BOMs) match spec - verified via live download.

Minor observation (not urgent): POST /purchasing-plan/generate returns job_id=200 immediately even for a malformed target_month, deferring validation to the async job/status poll rather than failing fast with 400/422 at request time. Functionally fine (UI surfaces the error via job status polling) but slightly non-RESTful; not required to fix given the existing async job architecture.

success_rate.backend: 100% (generate w/ invalid month, past month 2020-01, BOM search all verified via curl)
success_rate.frontend: 90% (search, highlighting, no-match, month-picker, disabled states, export/download all passed; sort-header caret UI passed; sort+expand interaction found a real bug)

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: BomExplorerPage.js identifies tree nodes for expand/collapse purposes purely by their POSITIONAL path in the currently rendered array (e.g., collectExpandableKeys(result.tree) and flattenVisibleTree both generate keys like '1', '2', '1-0' based on array index at each level). sortTree() is a pure function that returns a NEW node array with siblings re-ordered by the chosen field/direction; it does not preserve original array positions. Because expandedKeys (a Set of these positional strings) is stored in component state and NOT recomputed/remapped when sortConfig changes, a node's expand state effectively transfers to whichever OTHER node happens to land at that same index after sorting, instead of following the original node. Fix should use a stable identity for keys, e.g., derive path from product_id chain (e.g. 'P26584>P26688') instead of sibling index, so expand state survives reordering.
